cards.back: When a seed starts to grow into a new plant.
cards.say: germination. When a seed starts to grow into a new plant.

cards.front: What do seeds need to germinate?
cards.back: Water, warmth and oxygen. Most seeds do not need light or soil to start growing.
cards.say: What do seeds need to germinate? Water, warmth and oxygen. Most seeds do not need light or soil to start growing.

cards.back: A very young plant that has just grown from a seed.
cards.say: seedling. A very young plant that has just grown from a seed.

cards.back: The stages a living thing goes through from the start of its life until it makes new young.
cards.say: life cycle. The stages a living thing goes through from the start of its life until it makes new young.

cards.front: List the stages of a flowering plant's life cycle.
cards.back: Seed, germination, seedling, adult plant with flowers, pollination, fertilisation, seeds and fruit, seed dispersal.
cards.say: List the stages of a flowering plant's life cycle. Seed, germination, seedling, adult plant with flowers, pollination, fertilisation, seeds and fruit, seed dispersal.

cards.back: When pollen is moved from the stamen of one flower to the stigma of another flower of the same kind.
cards.say: pollination. When pollen is moved from the stamen of one flower to the stigma of another flower of the same kind.

cards.back: Tiny grains made in the anther. They contain the male sex cells.
cards.say: pollen. Tiny grains made in the anther. They contain the male sex cells.

cards.back: An animal, such as a bee or a bird, that carries pollen from flower to flower.
cards.say: pollinator. An animal, such as a bee or a bird, that carries pollen from flower to flower.

cards.back: A sweet liquid made by flowers. It attracts insects.
cards.say: nectar. A sweet liquid made by flowers. It attracts insects.

cards.back: They have bright petals, a scent and nectar. Their pollen is sticky or spiky so it sticks to insects.
cards.say: How are insect-pollinated flowers adapted? They have bright petals, a scent and nectar. Their pollen is sticky or spiky so it sticks to insects.

cards.back: They have small dull petals, hanging anthers and feathery stigmas. They make lots of light pollen.
cards.say: How are wind-pollinated flowers adapted? They have small dull petals, hanging anthers and feathery stigmas. They make lots of light pollen.

cards.back: When the male sex cell from a pollen grain joins the female sex cell inside an ovule. A seed starts to form.
cards.say: fertilisation. When the male sex cell from a pollen grain joins the female sex cell inside an ovule. A seed starts to form.

cards.front: After fertilisation, what does the ovule become?
cards.back: A seed.
cards.say: After fertilisation, what does the ovule become? A seed.

cards.front: After fertilisation, what does the ovary become?
cards.back: A fruit, which holds the seeds.
cards.say: After fertilisation, what does the ovary become? A fruit, which holds the seeds.

cards.back: Spreading seeds away from the parent plant.
cards.say: seed dispersal. Spreading seeds away from the parent plant.

cards.front: Why do plants disperse their seeds?
cards.back: So the new plants do not have to compete with their parent for light, water and space.
cards.say: Why do plants disperse their seeds? So the new plants do not have to compete with their parent for light, water and space.

cards.back: By wind. Each seed has light, fluffy hairs like a parachute.
cards.say: How are dandelion seeds dispersed? By wind. Each seed has light, fluffy hairs like a parachute.

cards.back: By animals. The seeds have tiny hooks that stick to fur.
cards.say: How are burdock seeds dispersed? By animals. The seeds have tiny hooks that stick to fur.

cards.back: By water. They float in the sea and can wash up on faraway beaches.
cards.say: How are coconuts dispersed? By water. They float in the sea and can wash up on faraway beaches.

cards.front: How do pea pods spread their seeds?
cards.back: The pod dries and splits open suddenly, flinging the seeds out.
cards.say: How do pea pods spread their seeds? The pod dries and splits open suddenly, flinging the seeds out.

cards.front: How does an animal that eats a fruit spread its seeds?
cards.back: The seeds pass out in its droppings, often far from the parent plant.
cards.say: How does an animal that eats a fruit spread its seeds? The seeds pass out in its droppings, often far from the parent plant.

cards.front: Which part of a germinating seed grows first?
cards.back: The root. It grows down to take in water.
cards.say: Which part of a germinating seed grows first? The root. It grows down to take in water.
